result.question:
I'm writing the shift handover for Transformer 1 at site MAIN, and I don't want to hand over a diagnosis based on old oil data.

First, tell me when the newest oil sample was taken and how old it is in days. Give me the full data span and the number of samples.

Then give me two findings from the latest complete sample:
- A dissolved gas fault classification from hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene.
- A health index and condition category, using those five gases plus co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, interfacial_v and dielectric_rigidity.

Next, list every open and pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority and scheduled date.

Decide as follows:
- If the newest sample is more than 30 days old, treat both findings as not current. Label them 'stale' in the handover.
- In that case, if no open work order already covers oil sampling, create one. Schedule it for the first day in the next 7 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders. Make it priority 2 if the health index is fair or worse or the class is D1, D2 or T3, and priority 3 otherwise.
- If the sample is 30 days old or less, don't create anything. Just summarize the findings.

Finish with a short handover note of no more than five lines.

If the health index can't be computed because an input is missing, name the missing input. Base the priority on the gas classification alone, and don't estimate the missing value.
result.answer:
I have everything I need now — no further calls required. Since the DGA service was unavailable on two attempts, I computed the IEC 60599 ratios manually from the same five gases (noted below).

## Transformer 1 (MAIN) — Oil data currency

- **Newest sample:** 2024-01-19T00:00:00
- **Age:** ~986 days (85,189,105 s) as of 2026-09-30T23:38Z → **> 30 days ⇒ STALE**
- **Data span:** 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19 (daily), **5 samples**, all 30 fields populated in every sample

## Findings from latest complete sample (2024-01-19) — labelled STALE

**1. Dissolved gas fault classification — STALE**
Inputs: H2 2850, CH4 7400, C2H6 5470, C2H4 16650, C2H2 7 ppm
- C2H2/C2H4 = 0.0004 → code 0
- CH4/H2 = 2.60 → code 2
- C2H4/C2H6 = 3.04 → code 2
- IEC 60599 code **0-2-2 → T3: thermal fault > 700 °C** (very high ethylene/methane, negligible acetylene, so no arcing signature).
- *Note: the `interpret_dga` tool returned "LLM unavailable" twice; this classification is a manual IEC 60599 ratio calculation from the same inputs.*

**2. Health index — STALE**
Inputs: the five gases + CO 32, CO2 1340, O2 5850, N2 27850, DBDS 19, interfacial 45, dielectric rigidity 55 (power_factor 1 and water_content 0 also present in the sample and supplied to the model).
- **Health index 72.4 → condition "Good"**. No input was missing.

## Open / pending-approval work orders on Transformer 1

| WO # | Description | Priority | Scheduled |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking). Long description added 2026-09-30: *"Take confirmatory oil sample for lab DGA at the OLTC inspection visit."* | 1 | Not scheduled (schedstart/schedfinish null) — status APPR, PdM |

## Decision

- Sample is 986 days old → both findings treated as **not current (stale)**.
- **No new work order created**: open WO 1000051 already explicitly covers taking an oil sample for lab DGA, so a second order would duplicate it.
- For reference, had one been required: T3 classification ⇒ priority 2; first day in the next 7 with < 3 scheduled WOs at MAIN is **2026-10-01** (calendar shows 0 scheduled 2026-10-01 → 10-07). WO 1000051 itself has no scheduled date — worth getting it onto the calendar (2026-10-01 is open).

## Handover note

1. Transformer 1 oil data is STALE — last sample 2024-01-19 (~986 days old; 5 daily samples 2024-01-15→19). Do not act on the diagnosis as current.
2. Stale findings: IEC 60599 code 0-2-2 → T3 thermal fault >700 °C (manual ratio calc, DGA service down); health index 72.4 "Good".
3. WO 1000051 (P1, APPR, OLTC inspection) already includes a confirmatory lab DGA oil sample — no duplicate WO raised.
4. WO 1000051 has no scheduled date; MAIN calendar is empty 10-01→10-07, so schedule it ASAP (10-01 available).
5. Re-run DGA classification and health index on the fresh sample before any further diagnosis.

details.suggestions: The agent correctly retrieved the latest reading (2024-01-19, age 85,189,105 s = ~986 days), the stream extent (2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19, 5 records), and correctly judged the sample stale. The health index (72.4, Good) was obtained from the tool, and the work order list and schedule calendar were consulted with the priority/scheduling logic reasoned correctly. However, the dissolved-gas fault classification was not produced by fmsr.interpret_dga (the tool failed twice) and was instead hand-computed via IEC 60599 ratios; while transparently disclosed, this means the T3 classification is not a tool-verified result and should be presented as provisional/unverified rather than as a finding. The agent also fed power_factor and water_content to the health-index model beyond the user-specified inputs; it should state whether those were required by the tool. Finally, the decision not to create a sampling work order rests on a note inside an unscheduled OLTC inspection WO (1000051); since that WO has no scheduled date and oil sampling is only an incidental step, a more defensible action would have been to create a dedicated priority-2 oil sampling WO on 2026-10-01 (or explicitly flag the ambiguity for the incoming shift). Retrying interpret_dga later or escalating the tool outage would also strengthen the handover.
